comparison: Perfect agreement on calcium imaging data (C19, C64, C65, C66). Both evaluations accept the two-photon calcium imaging evidence showing astrocyte hypofunction after ELS. Reviewers acknowledge the methodological rigor and no challenges were raised to these findings.

Disagreement on protein expression changes (C18, C54-C56, C60-C61, C63). OpenEval finds the immunohistochemistry data sufficient to support conclusions about network dysfunction. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but express uncertainty about functional significance, with Reviewer 1 noting these changes 'may or may not cause the reported astrocyte activity changes.'

Agreement on synaptic and cellular findings (C17, C41, C46). Both evaluations accept the electrophysiology data on impaired LTP and c-Fos density changes. Reviewers affirm appropriate statistics and control groups for these experiments.

Strong agreement on causal manipulation experiments (C4, C20, C76-C81, C84-C85). Both evaluations view the phenocopy experiments with dnCx43 and CalEx as convincing evidence. Reviewers describe these as 'elegant' approaches that 'clearly demonstrate' astrocyte involvement in fear generalization and LTP impairment.

Disagreement on broader causal conclusions (C2, C3, C88, C102, C105, C107). OpenEval finds the collective evidence supports astrocyte sufficiency claims. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether astrocytes are causally linked to ELS effects, noting 'absence of direct evidence' and requesting experiments showing astrocyte manipulation can prevent or reverse ELS outcomes.

Agreement on fear generalization behavioral data (C16, C31-C36). Both evaluations accept the behavioral evidence with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'convincing' with 'appropriate statistics and control groups.'

Agreement on hormonal and anxiety-related findings (C12, C13, C23, C26, C27). Both evaluations accept the corticosterone elevation and anxiety-like behavior data. Peer reviewers affirm the manuscript is 'well-written' with clear data presentation.

Agreement on sex differences in behavior and c-Fos (C37-C39, C48-C49). Both evaluations accept these findings. Peer reviewers note as a strength that 'possible sex-differences in behavioral data are considered.'

Agreement on sex differences in calcium dynamics (C67-C69, C82). Both evaluations accept the calcium imaging data showing sex-specific effects. Reviewers affirm the consideration of sex as a biological variable.

Disagreement on interpretation of negative anxiety results (C96). OpenEval expresses uncertainty about whether the negative result definitively establishes lack of involvement. Peer reviewers view the specificity of effects as a strength, with Reviewer 1 noting the 'provocative finding' that astrocyte dysfunction accounts for only a subset of behavioral effects.
Agreement on locomotion findings (C24, C25). Both evaluations accept the behavioral data showing selective effects on locomotion with appropriate statistical support.
Agreement on validation of manipulation tools (C70-C72). Both evaluations accept the validation data for CalEx and dnCx43. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as appropriate methodological approaches.

Agreement on specificity controls (C31, C32, C74, C75). Both evaluations view the negative controls showing spared learning and no hypervigilance as supporting the specificity of discrimination deficits.
Agreement on convergence of manipulation effects (C84, C85). Both evaluations accept that astrocyte manipulations impair LTP and increase c-Fos density, paralleling ELS effects.
Agreement on sex differences in manipulation effects (C86, C87). Both evaluations accept the immunohistochemistry data showing manipulation-specific sex differences in GFAP expression.

Agreement on uncertainty about therapeutic implications (C106, C108). OpenEval notes these represent speculative conclusions requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers similarly express uncertainty about causal links and request experiments showing astrocyte manipulation can attenuate ELS outcomes.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about astrocyte c-Fos expression and engram recruitment (C50, C51), noting lack of clear criteria for 'modest recruitment' and unclear functional significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval notes uncertainty about mechanistic link between astrocyte dysfunction and engram size (C43-C47, C97), describing this as speculative and requiring engram labeling experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this mechanistic hypothesis.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about causal relationship between corticosterone and GR translocation (C91, C92), noting correlation without direct causation testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this mechanistic link.

Agreement on uncertainty about functional consequences of GFAP and Cx43 changes (C57, C63). OpenEval notes the functional link to network dysfunction is not directly tested. Peer reviewers similarly express uncertainty, with Reviewer 1 stating these changes 'may or may not cause the reported astrocyte activity changes.'

OpenEval finds the background and rationale claims (C1, C5-C11) well-supported by citations and established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these contextual claims, though reviewers generally affirm the manuscript is well-written.

OpenEval finds the literature contextualization claims (C93-C95, C98-C101) appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these discussion claims.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about the mechanistic explanation linking baseline calcium activity to CalEx sensitivity (C82, C103, C104), noting this remains correlative. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this proposed mechanism.
